text:
maria: heads-up — Prod canary deploys for model-serving are failing to come up in eu-west-1. Started ~10m ago after the gitops sync. Pods are Pending with `0/6 nodes` and no GPU nodes getting claimed.
maria: logs show Helm rendered manifest without the `nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia` block — looks like the helm values file was missing the decrypted secret value that normally flips that on.
josh: ugh. so SOPS decryption didn't happen in the pipeline? any error from the gitops sync?
maria: argo shows a successful sync, but the commit it applied had the sealedsecret placeholder still encrypted. our kustomize overlay renders `values-prod.yaml` with a `{{ .Values.gpu.enabled }}` that defaulted to false because the SOPS value was not present.
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Applied commit 7f3a2d4 to clusters/prod/eu-west-1 — sync complete. (no alerts) :white_check_mark:
khoa: quick theory: sealedsecrets CI job that decrypts -> stores plain yaml in the repo failed upstream, so the manifest in git never had gpu=true. Need to check the secrets pipeline logs (sops-vault-sync job).
lina: I saw a transient Vault auth error earlier from the sops runner: `permission denied: vault kv get secret/data/ci/helm/prod`. That would cause the sops step to leave the encrypted payload in place.
josh: can we hotfix the canary without a full secrets pipeline rerun? we need GPUs available asap for the batch test.
maria: two options: 1) manually patch the applied helm release in-cluster with nodeSelector (kubectl patch) — quick but brittle, will be overwritten on next sync; 2) re-run the secrets job + create a new commit so GitOps applies the correct manifest — slower (5-10m) but durable.
khoa: also consider an initContainer that fetches runtime secrets from Vault and writes a values file — that avoids relying on repo-level decryption ordering, but needs RBAC for the service account. Feels like an architectural change.
lina: for immediate: I'm going to run the sops-vault-sync job locally against prod secrets to confirm Vault auth and re-encrypt the sealedsecret output. If I can push a fix commit we can let Argo apply it and un-stall the pods.
josh: while that's in flight, I'll patch a single canary deployment to unblock tests. I'll add a comment to the PR so we revert the patch after the proper sync.
maria: note: root cause might be Vault token TTL rotation — CI runner used a cached token that expired mid-job. We'll need to rotate to short-lived dynamic tokens and improve retry logic.
khoa: agree. Action items: 1) lina -> re-run sops sync and push commit (ETA 10m). 2) josh -> temporary kubectl patch to canary (ETA 5m). 3) infra -> add retry + backoff in sops runner and log the Vault error as high severity. 4) engineering -> evaluate initContainer approach for long term.
lina: starting sops run now, watching auth logs.
maria: fyi cost note — when pods stay Pending the cluster autoscaler sometimes spins up CPU nodes (because other pods trigger scale) which increases spend. fixing ordering will avoid unnecessary non-GPU node churn.
josh: noted. will keep an eye on node creation in eu-west-1.
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] New commit 7f3a2d4-revert-wip pushed by lina — Argo sync queued.
khoa: once this is closed we should add a pre-sync check in our gitops pipeline: fail the sync if any sealedsecret in the commit is still encrypted, or add a hook that validates `values-prod.yaml` has `gpu.enabled: true/false` explicitly (no templated defaulting).
maria: +1. Also add an alert to SRE dashboard for Vault auth errors from the sops runner (SLA: 3 retries then pager).
lina: update: sops run succeeded locally, pushed commit `7f3a2d4-fix-secrets`. Argo picked it up and started apply.
josh: patch reverted after canary came up — pods Scheduled and GPUs allocated. Running batch smoke now. :thumbsup:
maria: closing loop: I'll open an RFC for the initContainer pattern and the pre-sync check. Thanks all for quick triage.
